issues.description: Class/Type mismatch: The exercise expects a Meal class (constructor Meal(String, String[]), getters) as shown in the problem statement UML and the solution, but the template repository contains an implemented Order class (Order.java) and an empty Meal.java. Problem statement: specifies class Meal with fields name:String and ingredients:String[] and uses Meal in examples. Template: provides src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java (concrete implementation) and an empty src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java. Solution: provides src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java implemented. This mismatch can confuse students about which class to implement/use and leads to inconsistent examples in Main and the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template repository consistent with the problem statement: either remove or rename the extraneous Order.java and add a Meal.java stub that matches the UML/signature used in the problem (public class Meal with a constructor Meal(String, String[]) and getters getName(), getIngredients()). Also update Main.java examples in the template to reference Meal instead of Order to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The exercise describes a Meal class (problem statement refers to class Meal with a constructor Meal(String, String[]) and uses the identifier 'Meal' throughout). In the template repository there is no implemented Meal class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java is empty) but there is an Order class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java) that has the same shape (name and ingredients). The solution repository implements Meal (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java). This inconsistent naming (problem expects 'Meal', template provides 'Order' and an empty Meal file, solution uses 'Meal') will confuse students: they will look for the Meal type required by the tasks and find only an Order class and an empty Meal.java, making it unclear which identifier to use and forcing renaming or duplication work.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Options: (a) Rename the template's Order class to Meal (move/rename src/de/tum/cit/ase/Order.java -> src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) and update any references (e.g., Main and comments) to use Meal; or (b) add a proper Meal class in the template matching the problem statement (copy the shape from Order.java into src/de/tum/cit/ase/Meal.java) and remove or adapt the existing Order.java so only the expected identifier remains. Ensure the template's Main and all instructions reference 'Meal' consistently so students can directly map the problem requirements to the starter code.
